title: Roubaix to Avenue Montaigne: the Engineer, the Bankrupt Textile Group, and the Assembly of LVMH
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Roubaix, birth in the wool city
stops.date_confidence: attested. en.wikipedia and fr.wikipedia, 'Bernard Arnault', both give 5 March 1949 at Roubaix, Nord. The LVMH governance biography, which would be the house source, timed out on two fetch attempts and could not be read.
stops.campa: Bernard Jean Étienne Arnault is born in Roubaix, in the Nord, a city built on wool and on the mills that comb and spin it. His father Jean runs Ferret-Savinel, a construction and public works firm; the engineering runs on both sides of the house. The Roubaix he is born into is already past its peak, the textile fortunes thinning, the brick courées emptying decade by decade. Nothing in the family suggests couture. What the boy is raised to inherit is a firm that pours reinforced concrete on public tenders.
suggested_refs: Roubaix and the Nord textile basin in decline, 1945-1970

stops.name: Lille, the two lycées and the concours
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the schools, inferred as to the date. en.wikipedia, 'Bernard Arnault': educated at Lycée Maxence Van Der Meersch and Lycée Faidherbe in Lille; fr.wikipedia lists him among Faidherbe's alumni. No source gives the years, so the date is an ordering device defaulted to 01-01. The coordinate is Faidherbe's own, 9 rue Armand-Carrel, per fr.wikipedia; an earlier working coordinate placed the school 2.5 km away near the Grand-Place and is discarded.
stops.campa: He is schooled in Lille, at the Lycée Maxence Van Der Meersch and then at the Lycée Faidherbe on the rue Armand-Carrel, near the Porte de Douai. Faidherbe runs the classes préparatoires that feed the grandes écoles, a machine for entrance examinations: two years of mathematics and physics at a pace built to break most of the candidates, aimed at a single week of written and oral tests in Paris. He plays the piano seriously enough that the family weighs it against the engineering. He sits the concours and passes.
suggested_refs: Lycée Faidherbe, 9 rue Armand-Carrel, Lille, and its classes préparatoires

stops.name: Rue Descartes, the school on the mountain
stops.date_confidence: attested as to admission 1969 and graduation 1971 in mathematics and civil engineering (en.wikipedia and fr.wikipedia, 'Bernard Arnault'). The month is not recorded and is set to July as the ordinary end of the school year. The place is corrected: an earlier working file gave Palaiseau, which is anachronistic, since en.wikipedia, 'École Polytechnique', records the move from central Paris to Palaiseau in 1976. In 1969-1971 the school stood at 5 rue Descartes.
stops.campa: Admitted in 1969, he spends his two years at the École Polytechnique while the school still stands at 5 rue Descartes on the Montagne Sainte-Geneviève, a military academy in the middle of the Latin Quarter, five years before it decamps to the fields at Palaiseau. He is trained in mathematics and in civil engineering, the curriculum that has supplied France with its bridge builders, its artillery officers, and its state engineers since the Revolution. He graduates in 1971. He does not take a post in the state.
suggested_refs: The École Polytechnique at 5 rue Descartes, Paris 5e, before the 1976 removal to Palaiseau

stops.name: Roubaix, engineer in his father's firm
stops.date_confidence: attested that he joined Ferret-Savinel as an engineer in 1971 (en.wikipedia, 'Bernard Arnault') and that he married Anne Dewavrin in 1973. The internal promotions, construction director 1974 and chief executive 1977, come from the working dossier alone and no company history could be loaded to confirm them. Month defaulted.
stops.campa: He joins Ferret-Savinel as an engineer in the year he leaves the school. The work is site work: reinforced concrete, public tenders, the slow margins of construction in a region losing its industry. He moves up through it quickly, construction director within three years and chief executive by 1977. In 1973 he marries Anne Dewavrin. There is no name to sell here and no window to dress, only a payroll and a schedule of works. He is twenty-eight in the year the firm becomes his to run.
sources: working dossier, Ferret-Savinel career section, uncorroborated
suggested_refs: Ferret-Savinel, the Arnault family construction firm of the Nord

stops.name: Roubaix, the firm turned toward the sun
stops.date_confidence: contradiction carried, not resolved. Both Wikipedias agree he became president of Ferret-Savinel in 1978; en.wikipedia ends the presidency in 1984, fr.wikipedia runs it to 1995. Neither is preferred here. The renaming to Férinel and the pivot to holiday property come from the working dossier and could not be confirmed against a company record. Month defaulted.
stops.campa: At twenty-nine he becomes president of Ferret-Savinel and argues at once that construction is the wrong business to be in. The industrial building arm is sold. The company is turned toward holiday property and renamed Férinel: apartments and residences sold to people who want the sun rather than the site. The corporate shell is kept and the trade carried on inside it is exchanged, which is the manoeuvre he will use for the next fifty years. By the end of the decade the firm has money to move and he has not settled on where.
suggested_refs: Férinel, the holiday-property successor to Ferret-Savinel

stops.name: Palm Beach, the condominiums
stops.date_confidence: attested in outline by en.wikipedia, 'Bernard Arnault', which records the relocation to the United States after the 1981 Socialist victory and condominium development in Palm Beach. No Florida property record or contemporary press account could be fetched to fix the dates or the scale. Month set to June to follow the May 1981 election.
stops.campa: François Mitterrand wins in May and the Socialists come in with nationalisations on the programme. Arnault moves his wife and children to Florida and puts the Férinel method to work on the other side of the Atlantic, developing condominiums at Palm Beach. He is thirty-two years old, out of his country, and selling holiday flats to buyers who have never heard of his family firm or of the Nord. The venture does not prosper, and he will say very little about it in the decades afterwards. He is back in France within three years.
suggested_refs: Airy Routier's account of the failed Palm Beach venture, cited in fr.wikipedia

stops.name: Manhattan, the driver who knew the other name
stops.date_confidence: tradition, and self-created. The anecdote survives only in Arnault's own retellings in interviews. No witness, no date, no independent record; nothing was located this session and nothing is likely to exist. Date and place are ordering devices only, set inside the American years.
stops.campa: The story he will tell for the rest of his life is set in a New York taxi. He asks the driver whether he knows the name of the president of France. The driver does not. He knows Dior. Arnault has spent ten years in property and takes the exchange as a demonstration: a French name attached to a dress outlives a French name attached to a government, and travels further. It is the origin he chose for himself, and he has repeated it in interviews for forty years. The driver has never been named, and neither has the year.
sources: Arnault's own recurring interview anecdote, no independent attestation
suggested_refs: The taxi anecdote as it recurs across Arnault's interviews from the 1980s onward

stops.name: Rue de Sèvres, Le Bon Marché in the wreck of Boussac
stops.date_confidence: attested that Arnault acquired the insolvent Boussac Saint-Frères group in 1984 in a state-managed rescue, gaining Christian Dior and Le Bon Marché (en.wikipedia, 'Bernard Arnault'). Le Monde's contemporaneous 1987 account could not be fetched, the domain being blocked here. The 44-page plan and the 12,200-of-15,000 job pledge come from fakirpresse.info, a hostile source, and are attributed rather than adopted. Month defaulted. Coordinate inherited from christian_dior.journey.json's Paris department-store pin.
stops.campa: Marcel Boussac's textile empire has passed to the Willot brothers and from them into insolvency, and the French state wants a buyer who will keep the looms turning. Arnault comes back from Florida and takes Boussac Saint-Frères in a state-managed rescue, carrying a plan of forty-four pages that undertakes to preserve twelve thousand two hundred of the group's fifteen thousand jobs. Inside the group, almost incidentally, sit the department store Le Bon Marché on the rue de Sèvres and the couture house of Christian Dior. He has bought a bankrupt spinning conglomerate in order to reach a name.
sources: fakirpresse.info, 'Bernard Arnault: le mensonge originel de Boussac Saint-Frères'
suggested_refs: Le Bon Marché, 24 rue de Sèvres, and the Boussac Saint-Frères rescue file of 1984

stops.name: 30 Avenue Montaigne, at the head of Dior
stops.date_confidence: attested that Arnault became chief executive of Christian Dior in 1985 (en.wikipedia, 'Bernard Arnault'). The month is not recorded and is defaulted. Christian Dior and LVMH corporate history pages returned 403 or timed out. The coordinate is inherited byte-identical from christian_dior.journey.json, stop '30 Avenue Montaigne, the house opens'. The quote is authentic but of 2008, twenty-three years later, and is placed here for its content, not as anything said at the time.
stops.campa: He takes the chief executive's chair at Christian Dior, in the grey and white house at 30 avenue Montaigne that Dior opened in 1946 on Marcel Boussac's money and left in 1957 by dying. He inherits the founder's name and the licensing structure raised over it after the founder's death, and forms the principle he will apply everywhere afterwards: one owner holds the design, the making, the image and the shop. A house that licenses its name out to strangers is spending its own capital. Arnault was eight years old the autumn Dior died.
stops.quote: Être insatisfait est une des conditions pour se remettre en question sur tout et tout le temps.
stops.quote_source: Marc Baudriller, 'L'empire Bernard Arnault', Challenges no. 116, 20-26 March 2008, p. 71, quoted at fr.wikiquote.org
suggested_refs: The house of Christian Dior at 30 avenue Montaigne, opened 1946 on Boussac capital

stops.name: Flixecourt, the mills of the Somme
stops.date_confidence: contested and attributed. The February 1985 job-shedding at the Bâcherie and ACM plants and the figure of some 3,000 posts in a year come from fakirpresse.info, founded by François Ruffin, who is a party to the quarrel and not a neutral witness; treated as reconstruction. The 9,000 layoffs over two years and the resulting nickname are attested by en.wikipedia, 'Bernard Arnault'. Coordinate corrected to en.wikipedia, 'Flixecourt', 50.0136/2.0819, from a working value 1.1 km off.
stops.campa: Two months after the takeover the Bâcherie and ACM plants at Flixecourt begin shedding workers. This is jute and linen country: the Saint brothers' weaving works employed fourteen thousand people in the town before the first war. Within a year some three thousand posts are gone across the group, and within two years nine thousand. The mills the plan undertook to protect are sold or shut. Boussac returns to profit in 1987. In the Somme, and then in the Paris press, he acquires the name the Terminator.
sources: fakirpresse.info, 'Bernard Arnault: le mensonge originel de Boussac Saint-Frères'
suggested_refs: Airy Routier, L'Ange exterminateur, the biography whose title attaches to this period

stops.name: Paris, Moët Hennessy joins Louis Vuitton
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the year: LVMH is created in 1987 by the merger of Moët Hennessy and Louis Vuitton (en.wikipedia, 'Bernard Arnault'). The month is not fixed in any source read here and is set to June as an ordering device. The Racamier invitation is attested inside the atlas by louis_vuitton.journey.json. Coordinate is the canonical Paris pin inherited byte-identical.
stops.campa: Moët et Chandon, Hennessy cognac, and the trunk house Louis Vuitton founded in 1854 are merged into one company. The two sides do not like each other. Henry Racamier, who married into the Vuitton family and turned a small leather firm into an international one, finds himself outnumbered on the board and goes looking for an ally with money. He invites in the man who has just taken Dior. Arnault does not behave like an ally. He buys alongside Guinness until the two of them hold some forty per cent of the merged company.
stops.quote: they have these two aspects, which may be contradictory: They are timeless, [and] they are at the utmost level of modernity.
stops.quote_source: Forbes India, 'The $100 Billion Man: How LVMH's Bernard Arnault Stitched Together A Giant Fortune', quoted at en.wikipedia, 'Bernard Arnault'
sources: louis_vuitton.journey.json, stop 'Paris, Arnault takes the chair'
suggested_refs: The 1987 Moët Hennessy and Louis Vuitton merger agreement

stops.name: 22 Avenue Montaigne, the chair
stops.date_confidence: contradiction carried, not resolved. en.wikipedia has Arnault elected chairman of LVMH's executive management board in January 1989; fr.wikipedia, cited in louis_vuitton.journey.json, has him officially patron only in April 1990. Both accounts stand and neither is adjudicated here. The precise day, 13 January, and the holding company Jacques Rober and the 43.5 per cent figure come from the working dossier; LVMH's own governance history timed out on repeated fetches.
stops.campa: The fight runs two years through the Paris commercial courts. Arnault builds a holding called Jacques Rober and a shareholding reported near forty-three and a half per cent, and the board that Racamier brought him onto elects him chairman of its executive management board. He is forty years old and five years out of the Boussac rescue, and the group he now runs is the largest of its kind anywhere. Racamier leaves the company his wife's family founded and spends years litigating about it.
suggested_refs: The Racamier-Arnault litigation of 1988-1990 and the two accession dates the sources give

stops.name: Paris, the marriage to Hélène Mercier
stops.date_confidence: attested as to date and person: fr.wikipedia, 'Bernard Arnault', gives 23 September 1991 and describes Hélène Mercier as a pianiste québécoise. The venue is not attested anywhere reachable; a working file placed the wedding at Châteauneuf-de-Grasse and no source supports it, so the stop sits at the canonical Paris pin rather than at an invented church. The count of five children is confirmed by the Forbes profile's account of the 2022 Agache reorganisation.
stops.campa: He marries Hélène Mercier on the twenty-third of September. She is a concert pianist, québécoise, who performs in Europe and North America and keeps performing. Two more children come from this marriage, bringing the number to five across the two. All five will in time be written into the partnership that holds the family's shares, and into the running French commentary about which of them is being tested for what. Of the wedding itself the record gives a date and two names.
suggested_refs: Hélène Mercier-Arnault's recital and recording career

stops.name: Saint-Émilion, Cheval Blanc bought in his own name
stops.date_confidence: attested by en.wikipedia, 'Château Cheval Blanc': Arnault and Albert Frère bought the estate personally in 1998, and LVMH acquired Arnault's share in 2009. Month defaulted. Coordinate corrected to the same page's 44°55'10"N 0°11'21"W, about 3 km from a working value that sat toward Saint-Émilion town. A working file also staged a 2003 meeting with Vladimir Putin at the estate; nothing loadable records it and it is not staged here.
stops.campa: Arnault and the Belgian financier Albert Frère buy Château Cheval Blanc, premier grand cru classé of Saint-Émilion, in their own names and not through the group. It is a private holding: no campaign, no line in an annual report, two men on the right bank owning a vineyard between them. The estate makes what the estate makes; the quantity does not answer to a plan, and there is no version of it to license. LVMH acquires Arnault's half only in 2009, eleven years on.
suggested_refs: Château Cheval Blanc, Saint-Émilion, and the Frère-Arnault partnership of 1998

stops.name: Paris, the Gucci shares and the white knight
stops.date_confidence: attested in outline by en.wikipedia, 'Gucci' and 'Bernard Arnault': LVMH built about a third of the shares, PPR bought 40 per cent in March 1999 at $75 a share, LVMH was diluted to 20.7 per cent, and the affair settled in September 2001 with LVMH exiting at a reported profit near $700 million. A working file staged this at the Enterprise Chamber of the Amsterdam Court of Appeal, with an employee stock-ownership defence; en.wikipedia's account of the affair contains neither, so that courtroom scene is dropped and the stop sits at the canonical Paris pin. Day defaulted.
stops.campa: LVMH accumulates roughly a third of Gucci without declaring an intention, and Gucci's management refuses to be taken. In March François Pinault's PPR buys forty per cent of the company at seventy-five dollars a share, diluting LVMH to twenty point seven and installing itself as protector. From this the two great French fortunes are permanently opposed, luxury against luxury, and each will spend the next quarter century buying against the other. LVMH settles in September 2001 and sells out at a reported profit near seven hundred million dollars.
suggested_refs: The 1999-2001 Gucci takeover contest and the PPR white-knight purchase

stops.name: Mayfair, the auction house sold down
stops.date_confidence: attested by theartnewspaper.com, 'Bernard Arnault sells 70% of his stake in Phillips de Pury Luxembourg', fetched directly, for the March 2002 sale of 70 per cent to Simon de Pury and Daniella Luxembourg. The 1999 purchase is carried from the working dossier and was not separately re-verified. Day defaulted.
stops.campa: Arnault buys the auction house Phillips in 1999 and sets it against Christie's and Sotheby's, the two firms that have divided the salerooms of London and New York between them for more than two centuries. His method is to guarantee sellers their price in advance. Guarantees at that scale are a way of buying market share with cash, and the losses are heavy. In March 2002 he sells seventy per cent to Simon de Pury and Daniella Luxembourg, who put their own names on the door.
sources: theartnewspaper.com, 'Bernard Arnault sells 70% of his stake in Phillips de Pury Luxembourg'
suggested_refs: Phillips de Pury and Luxembourg, and the guarantee model in the 2000-2002 salerooms

stops.name: Massy, the Carrefour position
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The whole episode, the 9.8 per cent taken with Colony Capital near 47 euros in 2007 and the exit of the remaining 5.7 per cent at 16 euros in 2021, comes from the working dossier; Reuters, which reported the 2021 exit, is blocked to WebFetch in this environment and no substitute could be loaded. Month defaulted.
stops.campa: With Colony Capital he takes about nine point eight per cent of Carrefour, the hypermarket group, at some forty-seven euros a share, on the argument that the company's real estate is worth more than its trade. The plan does not work. Carrefour lives on volume at thin margin, which is the exact inverse of everything the luxury group is built on, and the shares fall and keep falling. He sells the last five point seven per cent in 2021 at sixteen euros. It takes him fourteen years to close the position.
sources: working dossier, Carrefour section, uncorroborated; reuters.com blocked to WebFetch here
suggested_refs: The Blue Capital vehicle of Arnault and Colony Capital in Carrefour, 2007-2021

stops.name: Rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré, the swaps on Hermès
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The October 2010 disclosure of about 17.1 per cent, the rise toward 23 per cent, and the family's defensive reorganisation are carried from the working dossier; LVMH's own publication on the settlement timed out on fetch and no primary filing was read. Day defaulted.
stops.campa: In October LVMH discloses that it holds about seventeen per cent of Hermès, assembled quietly through cash-settled equity swaps that carried no declaration duty until they were converted into shares. The holding will reach some twenty-three per cent. Arnault says he wishes only to be a supportive long-term shareholder, and in the rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré nobody accepts this. The Hermès family, still in command of the saddlery at number twenty-four, calls it an attack and locks more than half the capital into a holding company none of them can sell out of.
sources: working dossier, Hermès section; lvmh.com publication on the settlement timed out
suggested_refs: The Hermès family holding company H51 and the 2014 LVMH settlement

stops.name: Via dei Condotti, the Bulgari swap
stops.date_confidence: attested and corrected. en.wikipedia, 'Bulgari': the family sold its 50.4 per cent controlling stake in exchange for about 3 per cent of LVMH, an all-share deal valued at 4.3 billion euros or 6.0 billion dollars, completed 4 October 2011. en.wikipedia, 'Bernard Arnault', carries the $5.2 billion figure from the March 2011 announcement; the two pages disagree and both figures are given. The Via dei Condotti address is the historic flagship store, not a corporate headquarters, and the coordinate is set to the street rather than to Piazza di Spagna.
stops.campa: The Bulgari family gives up its fifty point four per cent controlling stake and takes about three per cent of LVMH in exchange, an all-share swap completed on the fourth of October. The value is put at four point three billion euros, and in dollars anywhere between five point two and six billion depending on which announcement is being quoted. The Roman jeweller keeps its flagship on the Via dei Condotti, a hundred metres below the Spanish Steps, and the family that founded it becomes a shareholder in the group that now owns their name.
stops.quote: In the 90s, I had the idea of a luxury group and at the time I was very much criticized for it. I remember people telling me it doesn't make sense to put together so many brands. And it was a success ... and for the last 10 years now, every competitor is trying to imitate, which is very rewarding for us. I think they are not successful but they try.
stops.quote_source: CNBC interview, 2018, quoted in The Fashion Law, 'LVMH: A Timeline Behind the Building of a Conglomerate'
suggested_refs: The Bulgari flagship at Via dei Condotti 10, Rome

stops.name: Place de la Bourse, the regulator's maximum fine
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The AMF sanction decision SAN-2013-15 was reached at amf-france.org but only header metadata was retrievable; the substantive text of the ruling could not be extracted, so the 8 million euro figure and the 25 June 2013 date are carried from the working dossier rather than read from the decision itself.
stops.campa: The sanctions commission of the Autorité des marchés financiers fines LVMH eight million euros, then the maximum penalty it is permitted to impose, for failing to disclose the build-up of the Hermès position. The finding is that the swap structure kept the reportable holding below the declaration thresholds while the economic exposure was being assembled underneath it, out of sight of the market and of the family whose company was being bought. LVMH disputes the reasoning in public and does not appeal. The decision is registered as SAN-2013-15.
sources: amf-france.org, sanction decision SAN-2013-15, metadata only
suggested_refs: AMF sanction decision SAN-2013-15, 25 June 2013

stops.name: Paris, the financial dailies bought
stops.date_confidence: attested that Arnault bought La Tribune in 1993 and Les Échos in 2007 (en.wikipedia, 'Bernard Arnault'), and that the family holding also owns Le Parisien and Paris Match (fr.wikipedia, 'Bernard Arnault'). Paris Match was acquired from Lagardère only in 2024 and is dated accordingly, not folded back into the 2007 picture. Month set to November as the ordering point of the Échos sale; the day is not fixed here. Canonical Paris pin.
stops.campa: He has owned La Tribune since 1993. In 2007 he buys Les Échos, the country's leading business daily, and its journalists strike against the sale on the ground that a paper reporting on the luxury industry cannot belong to the largest luxury group in the world. Le Parisien follows, and in 2024 Paris Match, bought from Lagardère: a French reader can go from the business pages to the celebrity weekly without leaving his property. The sale of Les Échos goes through, and he grants the newsroom an ethics charter.
suggested_refs: The 2007 Les Échos strike and the ethics charter granted to its newsroom

stops.name: Élysée Palace, witness at the president's wedding
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. That Arnault was a witness at Nicolas Sarkozy's marriage to Carla Bruni on 2 February 2008 is very widely reported but was not confirmed by any source loadable this session; the venue likewise could not be independently fixed. Carried as tradition.
stops.campa: Nicolas Sarkozy marries Carla Bruni on the second of February, three months after they met, and Arnault stands as one of the witnesses to the marriage of a sitting president. Access of this kind is not a scandal in France; it is the ordinary condition of a very large company. He has been on working terms with governments of both descriptions for a quarter of a century: the Boussac rescue was arranged under a Socialist administration, he will publish for Macron in 2017, and he will attend two American presidential inaugurations.
sources: working dossier, politics section, not independently confirmed
suggested_refs: Press accounts of the Sarkozy-Bruni civil marriage, 2 February 2008

stops.name: Brussels, the naturalisation file
stops.date_confidence: attested, with a date correction. The application became public in September 2012, not December: fr.wikipedia, 'Bernard Arnault', dates the Libération reaction to September 2012, the negative opinion of the Brussels parquet to January 2013, and the withdrawal to April 2013. A working file gave a December 2012 disclosure, which cannot precede a September 2012 reaction. The ground of the parquet's opinion is not stated on the page and the three-years-residency reason is unverified. Day defaulted.
stops.campa: François Hollande has campaigned on a top income tax rate of seventy-five per cent. In September it emerges that Arnault has applied for Belgian nationality. He answers that the application has nothing to do with tax, that he will remain a French tax resident, and that he is not surrendering his French passport. The parquet of Brussels returns a negative opinion in January. In April 2013 he withdraws the request himself, in one sentence, and the file closes.
stops.quote: Je retire ma demande de nationalité belge
stops.quote_source: Agence France-Presse wire, 10 April 2013, cited at en.wikipedia, 'Bernard Arnault', ref. 84
suggested_refs: The Belgian naturalisation file of 2012-2013 and the opinion of the Brussels parquet

stops.name: Rue Béranger, the front page
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the cover and the advertising withdrawal by fr.wikipedia, 'Bernard Arnault', which dates the Casse-toi riche con! front page to September 2012 and cites both a 150,000 and a 700,000 euro figure for the advertising lost; the two figures are given and not adjudicated. The lawsuit and its abandonment come from the working dossier; theguardian.com is blocked to WebFetch here. Coordinate is Libération's 2012 address, 11 rue Béranger, 75003, not the 15th arrondissement offices it moved to in 2016.
stops.campa: Libération, then at 11 rue Béranger in the third arrondissement, runs the whole front page: a photograph of Arnault carrying a suitcase, under the words Casse-toi riche con! The phrase is Sarkozy's own insult to a farmer at the agricultural show, turned back on a different target. Arnault sues the paper for public insult and later abandons the claim. LVMH withdraws its advertising for the rest of the year, a loss the paper puts at between a hundred and fifty thousand and seven hundred thousand euros.
suggested_refs: Libération, front page of September 2012, and the withdrawal of LVMH advertising

stops.name: Paris, Merci Patron! and the men from the DGSI
stops.date_confidence: attested in outline by fr.wikipedia, 'Bernard Arnault': the 2016 Merci Patron! controversy, the family holding's press titles, and the record that in 2012 Arnault used Bernard Squarcini's DGSI channels in an extortion matter which ended in the dismissal of an LVMH employee. The allegation that the press holdings suppress coverage is reported by the source as critics' allegation and is not adjudicated. Month defaulted; canonical Paris pin.
stops.campa: François Ruffin releases Merci Patron!, a documentary in which he helps the Klur family, laid off from an LVMH-owned textile plant, extract compensation from the group by threatening it with embarrassment. The film draws hundreds of thousands of viewers and seeds a street movement. Four years earlier Arnault had gone through Bernard Squarcini's channels at the DGSI in an extortion matter that ended with an LVMH employee dismissed. Critics say the family's newspapers keep such stories small; the group says they do not.
suggested_refs: Merci Patron! (2016), directed by François Ruffin

stops.name: Bois de Boulogne, the glass sails open
stops.date_confidence: attested. en.wikipedia, 'Fondation Louis Vuitton': Gehry, 8 avenue du Mahatma-Gandhi, opened 20 October 2014, initial budget about 100 million euros against a final cost reported in May 2017 at 780 million. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from louis_vuitton.journey.json, stop 'Bois de Boulogne, the Fondation opens'; two other working values, 2.2649 and 2.2506, are discarded. The Cour des comptes figure of about 518 million euros in associated tax reductions is carried from the dossier and remains unverified.
stops.campa: Frank Gehry's building for the Fondation Louis Vuitton opens on the twentieth of October at 8 avenue du Mahatma-Gandhi, twelve curved glass sails over a white concrete iceberg at the edge of the Bois de Boulogne. Arnault commissioned it in 2006 against a budget of about a hundred million euros; the final construction cost is reported at seven hundred and eighty million. The President of the Republic attends the opening, and the collection hung inside is the founder's own. The building passes to the City of Paris after fifty-five years.
suggested_refs: The Cour des comptes report on the Fondation Louis Vuitton's cost and tax treatment

stops.name: Frewin Court, Oxford, an hour of questions
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The 2016 Oxford Union address is carried from the working dossier; the recording cited there was never fetched and no independent record of the event or its date was located. Month and day defaulted. Coordinate corrected to en.wikipedia, 'Oxford Union', Frewin Court OX1 3JB, about 400 m from a working value that fell east of Cornmarket Street.
stops.campa: He speaks at the Oxford Union, in the chamber off Frewin Court, and takes questions afterwards. The account he gives is the one he gives everywhere: that in the nineties nobody believed a set of luxury houses could be run as one group, that competitors have since spent a decade failing to copy it, that a great house must be simultaneously timeless and at the outer edge of the modern. The students ask about labour, about tax, about which of his children will follow him. He answers in English, evenly, for an hour.
sources: working dossier, Oxford Union section, unverified

stops.name: Paris, Pourquoi je vote Emmanuel Macron
